more white space.directive: Increase large uninterrupted white coloring regions. Remove secondary texture and nonessential interior marks without weakening the subject silhouette.

less detail.directive: Reduce tiny texture, decorative marks, and secondary line density. Keep only anatomy, story-critical props, and simple habitat cues.

simpler background.directive: Remove nonessential clutter and tiny texture while preserving strong habitat identity, environmental storytelling, perspective, and story-critical setting features. Simplify detail, not place.

clearer anatomy.directive: Correct anatomy and limb structure while preserving the successful pose and composition. Make joints, extremities, and body proportions easy to read.

stronger monster identity.directive: Strengthen the canonical silhouette, head features, body proportions, and signature anatomy so the creature is unmistakable at thumbnail size.

stronger outer contour.directive: Strengthen the main subject's outer contour and reduce competing interior lines so the creature separates clearly from the background.

lighter interior lines.directive: Reduce interior line weight and density while keeping the outer contour bold and readable.

story beat unclear.directive: Make the required story moment immediately readable through pose, cause-and-effect, and placement of the key prop or environmental interaction.

required prop missing.directive: Add the missing required prop in a clear, plausible position without redesigning successful anatomy, framing, or habitat.

pose too stiff.directive: Keep the composition but improve gesture, weight shift, and expression so the pose communicates the intended action rather than a static character portrait.

focal subject weak.directive: Make the monster immediately readable without weakening habitat identity. Reduce competing object scale, tangents, and unnecessary detail while preserving two to four strong environmental cues and the environmental interaction that supports the story.

composition wrong.directive: Rebuild the composition around three co-equal storytelling pillars: unmistakable monster identity, unmistakable environment identity, and one clear story moment. Use perspective and interaction to connect the creature to the place, with broad colorable shapes instead of filler clutter.

environment identity weak.directive: Strengthen the named habitat with two to four large, unmistakable environmental cues. Make the place identifiable at thumbnail size without adding decorative clutter.

environment generic.directive: Replace generic room or backdrop details with setting-specific architecture, terrain, furnishings, storage, hazards, vegetation, or lair features appropriate to the named habitat and fantasy context.

environment story disconnect.directive: Make at least one environmental feature directly participate in the story moment through cause-and-effect, use, movement, scale, concealment, danger, feeding, guarding, or habitation.

environment cluttered.directive: Reduce secondary environmental clutter while preserving the strongest habitat-defining features and all story-critical environmental interactions. Keep broad colorable shapes.

wrong environment.directive: Rebuild the scene in the correct named habitat using setting-appropriate architecture, terrain, furnishings, and props. The environment must be immediately recognizable and integrated with the monster's action.

modern setting drift.directive: Remove modern-looking domestic, industrial, or contemporary design cues that do not belong in the intended fantasy setting. Replace them with believable period-appropriate or fantastical equivalents.

wrong monster identity.directive: Regenerate from the canonical creature specification because the current subject is fundamentally off-model. Rebuild the head, silhouette, body proportions, posture, and signature anatomy so the creature is unmistakable at thumbnail size before preserving any scene details.

background reused.directive: Recompose the page using the assigned environment profile but a clearly different landmark, framing, depth structure, and monster/environment interaction from nearby pages. Do not reuse the same room, cave wall, seabed, corridor, or horizon layout.

objects too small.directive: Enlarge story-critical props and major environmental forms into a few bold, simple, easy-to-color shapes. Remove tiny secondary objects that create fiddly coloring regions.

monster too large.directive: Reduce the monster's page coverage enough for the assigned habitat, landmark, and story interaction to read clearly. Keep the creature substantial but restore meaningful environment around it.

environment objects too large.directive: Reduce any single foreground or environmental object that blocks monster anatomy or consumes the composition. Keep major objects large and easy to color, but subordinate them to the three-pillar scene balance.

too many tiny coloring regions.directive: Merge or remove micro-detail, repeated texture, tiny enclosed islands, and small decorative shapes. Preserve identity using fewer medium-to-large colorable regions.
